title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the first release whose average-weekly-earnings window CONTAINS the April 2027 month in which a 2026-10-28 Budget's employer-cost measures would take effect
source: EST: gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-june-2027, fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200) — the statutory pre-announcement register reads 'UK Labour Market June 2027', '15 June 2027 7:00am', status 'Confirmed', producer Office for National Statistics, designation 'Accredited official statistics', announcement page published 1 July 2026. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-labour-market-2027-03-16, 2026-09-10
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-labour-market-2027-03-16 LANE, 2026-09-10, AND IT IS FILED BECAUSE THAT LANE'S MEASUREMENT SAYS THIS IS THE VENUE THAT MATTERS AND THE ONE THE CHAIN HAS BEEN LOOKING AT IS NOT. Five documents in the UK labour chain have now reasoned about the first average-weekly-earnings window wholly after the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget; the 2027-03-16 lane confirmed that destination from the same-month anchor (the 19 March 2026 bulletin carries Nov 2025-Jan 2026) and then measured whether the milestone carries information. It does not. On the ONS's own private-sector regular-pay series (KAJ4, three-month-average year-on-year, seasonally adjusted, excluding arrears; ons.gov.uk timeseries /data, 304 observations from 2001), the change at the first-wholly-post-Budget boundary across the four Autumn Budgets with data was +0.2pp (2017), +0.4pp (2021), -0.3pp (2024) and -0.1pp (2025): signed mean +0.05pp, sign 2-2, mean absolute 0.25pp against an ordinary-month 0.183pp. WHAT DISTINGUISHES THIS RELEASE IS INCIDENCE, NOT ANNOUNCEMENT. UK employer-cost measures conventionally take effect the following April — the uk-labour-market-2026-11-17 lane's precedent, carried by reference: Autumn Budget 2024-10-30 raised secondary Class 1 NICs from 13.8% to 15% effective April 2025 — so a 2026-10-28 Budget bites in APRIL 2027. By the window rule the chain has now confirmed five times (headline AWE/LFS = the three months ending two months before the release month; vacancies end one month before; the payrolled flash is the month before), this release carries FEB-APR 2027 AWE/LFS, MAR-MAY 2027 vacancies and a MAY 2027 payroll flash — the first window containing that April. At the equivalent April-incidence boundary the same four Budgets gave 0.0pp (2018 APR), -0.1pp (2022 APR), -0.4pp (2025 APR) and -0.1pp (2026 APR): NO POSITIVE IN FOUR, directionally consistent where the announcement boundary is a coin flip. TWO HONEST QUALIFICATIONS SO THE ENTRY CANNOT BE OVER-READ. First, every one of those four deltas sits inside ordinary noise (control standard deviation 0.245pp) and a 3-of-3 sign test with one tie is p = 0.125 — suggestive, not significant; this is the right place to LOOK, not a signal to trade. Second, the 2026-10-28 Budget has not happened: as of this proposal it is 48 days in the future and its employer-cost measures are entirely unknown, so 'takes effect in April 2027' is a convention inferred from precedent and not a reading of any announced measure. WHY IT IS A PROPOSAL AND NOT A FORWARD TEST ON THE PROPOSING LEDGER: 2027-06-15 falls long after that event's own close-out window (closeOutWithinDays 6 from 2027-03-16), and the uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 lane banked the rule that a test scoring after its author's close-out leaves the Outcome cell for nobody to fill. Filing the venue instead hands the pre-derived question to the lane that will own it. TIERED LOW on the same argued grounds as every sibling: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol, no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
